Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.

Comments: Remote cloud only, no local hyperscale. N/A

revision_notes: No source was originally cited. Verified sources (Inflect data-centre directory, Dec 2025; TechnoMag, Jun 2025; Xalam Analytics data-centre market brief, Jul 2025) show Zimbabwe has no direct hyperscale cloud on-ramp but is served via a nearby regional availability zone in Johannesburg (same SADC sub-region), plus a new local Econet/Africa Data Centres facility (2025) delivering Google and Microsoft cloud services via partnership. This fits scale level 3 (regional AZ nearby) better than the original level 2 (distant regions only >100ms latency), so the score is revised upward from 2 to 3.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: No source was originally cited for the 'no requirements' score. Zimbabwe's Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] of 2021 (ss.28-29, Transborder Flow) restricts transfer of personal data outside Zimbabwe unless adequate protection is demonstrated and requires notification to the Data Protection Authority, confirmed by DLA Piper's Data Protection Laws of the World guide. This is a comprehensive, broadly-applicable requirement rather than an absence of rules, so the score is revised from 1 to 4.

revision_notes: No source was originally cited. Verified evidence shows several active hubs (Hypercube, Impact Hub Harare, iZone Hub, Eight2Five, Tech Hub Harare) and a government-backed National Venture Capital Fund (est. 2021, reactivated 2025), which would suggest 'Developing' (level 3); however Disrupt Africa's African Tech Startups Funding Report 2025 lists Zimbabwe as having no externally-tracked VC funding in 2025 (present in 2024, absent in 2025), consistent with 'Emerging' (level 2).
